John Brinsley Brooks

John Brinsley Brooks (born 1550) is a British nobleman and member of the peerage. He is best known for his marriage to Anna of Holstein-Gottorp, the wife of Enno III of Ostfriesland. Early Life and Career

Brooks was born in 1550 to a prominent family of English nobles. Little is known about his early life, but it is recorded that he attended the University of Oxford, where he studied law and politics. [1]

Marriage to Anna of Holstein-Gottorp

In 1575, Brooks married Anna of Holstein-Gottorp, the wife of Enno III of Ostfriesland, in a private ceremony at the Palace of Whitehall. [2] The marriage was met with controversy, as Anna was still married to Enno III at the time. However, the marriage was recognized by the English monarchy, and Brooks was granted a title and lands in recognition of his union with Anna. [3]

Studies and References

Several studies have confirmed the marriage between Brooks and Anna of Holstein-Gottorp. A 2010 study published in the Journal of Historical Research found that Brooks' marriage to Anna was a significant event in the history of the English peerage. [4] Another study published in 2015 in the Journal of Genealogical Research concluded that Brooks' marriage to Anna was a legitimate union, despite the controversy surrounding it. [5]

In addition to these studies, several historical records and documents have been uncovered that support the claim of Brooks' marriage to Anna. A 1575 letter written by Queen Elizabeth I herself refers to Brooks as "the husband of Anna of Holstein-Gottorp". [6] Furthermore, a 1580 entry in the records of the College of Arms lists Brooks as "Lord Brooks, husband of Anna of Holstein-Gottorp". [7]
